parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the binding energy of a nucleus.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A nucleus of uranium-235 absorbs a neutron and becomes unstable. It then undergoes a fission reaction. One possible reaction is

²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ¹⁴²₅₄Xe + ⁹⁰₃₈Sr + neutrons.
parts.text: Determine the number of neutrons produced in this fission reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Data for the binding energies per nucleon for this fission reaction are given in Table 8.1.

[[fig:f1]]

Calculate the energy released, in MeV, from the fission of one nucleus of uranium-235.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The isotope xenon-142 is unstable. The isotope xenon-132 is stable.

Suggest a reason why xenon-142 is unstable.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Xenon-142 decays into the isotope caesium-142.

A sample initially contains only nuclei of xenon-142. After a time equal to 6.0 s, the ratio $\frac{\text{number of decayed nuclei of xenon-142}}{\text{number of undecayed nuclei of xenon-142}}$ is equal to 31.

Calculate the half-life of xenon-142. Show your working.

figures.caption: Table 8.1
figures.alt: A table gives binding energy per nucleon in MeV: uranium-235, 7.59; xenon-142, 8.37; and strontium-90, 8.72.
